title: Projective-bundle morphisms are proper
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. If $f$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], meaning that $X$ is isomorphic over $S$ to a closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal E)$ for a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal E$, then $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Lemma 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper), together with Lemma 01WB (lemma-characterize-locally-projective) and Definition 01W8 (definition-projective).

proof.text: By [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], choose $P=\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$, its projection $\pi$, and a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ over $S$ with $f=\pi i$, absorbing the given isomorphism into $i$. Apply [lem-trf-projective-bundle-affine-presentations] to $\mathcal E$. Obtain an affine covering $(U_\alpha)$ and H-projective projections $\mathbf P_{U_\alpha}(\mathcal E|_{U_\alpha})\to U_\alpha$, together with finite generating sections and their closed embeddings into finite projective spaces.

source.place: Tags 01W8 (definition-projective) and 01WB (lemma-characterize-locally-projective), finite generators and local presentations

proof.text: For $U=U_\alpha$, the open-base clause of [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] (with $V=U$; it assumes only quasi-coherence of $\mathcal E$) identifies $P_U=\pi^{-1}(U)=P\times_SU$ canonically, over $U$, with $\mathbf P_U(\mathcal E|_U)$, carrying $\pi|_{P_U}$ to the projective-bundle projection; the relative Proj there is that of the canonical symmetric graded algebra, which is the algebra of [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] on every affine open. Precomposing the finite-space closed embedding $j_\alpha$ from Step 1 with this isomorphism preserves closed immersion: the underlying homeomorphism onto a closed subset and the surjective structure-sheaf map in [def-weil-closed-immersion] are composed with an isomorphism. Thus $P_U\to U$ equals the projective-space projection composed with a closed immersion, so it is H-projective by [def-kun-projective], and is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper].

source.place: Tag 01WB (lemma-characterize-locally-projective), proof: X_U a closed subscheme of P(E) over the affine U, closed immersion into P^n_R; Tag 01WC proof, properness of H-projective morphisms.

proof.text: Put $X_U=f^{-1}(U)$. Since $f=\pi i$, the inverse image under $i$ of the open subscheme $P_U$ is exactly $X_U$. Hence $i_U:X_U\to P_U$ is the base change of $i$ along $P_U\hookrightarrow P$, and is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The restriction of $f$ is $(\pi|_{P_U})i_U$. Step 2 and clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] make this composite proper. The opens $U$ cover $S$, so [lemma-nagata-projective-target-local] gives properness of $f$. This last application allows an infinite cover.

source.place: Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper), closed immersions, composition and locality; Tags 01QR, 01W5, 01W3 and 01W2

proof_origin.place: Tags 01WB and 01WC, proofs, using the open-base identification of projective bundles (lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry) and the finite-generating-section embedding of Tag 087S.
